items.name: Tencent Hy4
items.summary: Tencent launched the full Hy4 model on November 4, a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that adds native visual understanding and computer-use abilities to the Hunyuan line for the first time. It can read images and operate software via command-line and graphical interfaces, and is live through Tencent Cloud TokenHub, OpenRouter and Tencent's own apps, with open weights promised soon.

items.name: MiniMax M3
items.summary: MiniMax unveiled M3 on November 3, billed as the first open-weight model to combine frontier coding and agentic capabilities, a 1-million-token context window and native multimodality. Built on its MiniMax Sparse Attention architecture, it is aimed at coding assistants and autonomous multi-step workflows, with full open-sourcing on Hugging Face and GitHub to follow.

items.name: Sarvam Prism
items.summary: Sarvam AI released Prism on November 3, an open-weight decision model built on its Sarvam 105B base that evaluates predefined options in a single forward pass instead of generating token by token. It answers in a reported 44 milliseconds on one NVIDIA B200 GPU with a 71.8 average across three benchmarks, and its Apache 2.0 weights let enterprises run it on their own infrastructure.

items.name: Deep Principle Hydrogen-1.0
items.summary: Deep Principle launched Hydrogen-1.0 on November 2, a 753-billion-parameter open-weight scientific foundation model for chemistry, materials science and life sciences, post-trained from Z.ai's GLM-5.3 on lab records and discovery trajectories. Its MIT-licensed weights, 1-million-token context and reported edge over GPT-6 Astra on FrontierScience-Research make it a notable specialist challenger to general frontier models.

items.name: Google Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28 as its strongest model to date, built for cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic engineering, ranking first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 with a score of 59. Initial access is limited to a subset of vetted cybersecurity defenders through Google's Fairwind Program, with wider developer and consumer availability still undated.
